_toc: how_to_score / severity — PASS/FAIL/NA mechanics; hard vs soft.
scale_bridge — how PASS/FAIL maps onto the Critic's 1-7 visual_design scale + the special caps (any_hard_fail, interactive_set_hard_fail, credibility_baseline_cap, chart_signature_floor).
lens_map / _sources — which Auditor lens scores which group; the upstream license-clean sources.
groups.typography — TYP1-5 (display+body, contrast, measure, balance, tabular nums).
groups.color — COL1-5 (themed tokens, one data scale, AA contrast, colorblind-safe, accent marks the datum).
groups.layout_spacing — LAY1-7 (reading column, full-bleed rare, focal centerpiece, section rhythm, vertical rhythm, image-size cap, decorative-layers-no-data-*).
groups.chart_quality — CHT1-5 (annotate the datum, direct labels, de-clutter, right chart type, every chart renders).
groups.motion — MOT1-6 (reduced-motion, no autoplay sound, no AI-slop pulse, no motion-on-mount, no fade/scale spam, no reveal-hides-content).
groups.accessibility — A11Y1-5 (alt text, focus ring, keyboard ops, semantic structure, 44px targets).
groups.anti_template — ANT1-5 (no purple hero, not all-centered, no even-card-grid, no default-font, applied-regardless-of-subject).
_note: Shared design-quality rubric. Authoring SOT for Designer/Programmer; scoring SOT for the Auditor vision lenses and the Critic visual_design dimension. Each criterion is PASS/FAIL; a vision agent or LLM can score it.
how_to_score: Each criterion PASS/FAIL/NA. A group fails if any HARD criterion fails. Vision agents score visual groups from screenshots; source-detectable ones (detect:source) are grep/LLM-checkable. NA only when the page genuinely lacks the element (e.g. no map, no audio, no interactive); never NA to dodge a present element.

severity.hard: one fail caps visual_design at 3 (Critic) / is a high-severity Auditor finding
severity.soft: advisory; multiple soft fails together cap at 3

scale_bridge._note: How PASS/FAIL maps onto the Critic's integer 1-7 visual_design scale (skills/data2story/critic/references/rubric.json). This rubric does not invent a new scale; it gates the existing one.
scale_bridge.interactive_set_hard_fail: A purposeless supporting playground (PIT-30: no INFORM/IMMERSE purpose, re-teaches the hero, or the reader produces nothing), a dead control / inert or recompute-disagreeing playground (PIT-31/PIT-32, real-browser playtest), a playground with no JS/CDN-off fallback (PIT-33), or a widget-pile with no clear hero (PIT-34) is an ANT5/LAY3-class HARD fail — it trips `any_hard_fail` and caps visual_design at 3 (a hero-less pile also caps insight_value at 3 per critic rubric R8). Abundance never raises the score; the gate caps each unearned interactive exactly like decorative media.
scale_bridge.credibility_baseline_cap: An accuracy / skill / 'how good is the model' claim shown WITHOUT an honest baseline comparison caps the CREDIBILITY dimension (critic rubric data_method_transparency / claim_data_alignment) at 3 — mirroring `any_hard_fail` but on credibility, not visual_design. A headline like 'the model called 14 of 28' or 'it is accurate' means nothing until it is lined up against the dumbest reasonable forecaster (a naive base-rate / market / consensus benchmark), with the BETTER value marked per metric EVEN WHEN THE BASELINE WINS (see exemplars/cinematic_flagship.md E2 + interaction_playbook.json content_patterns.model_vs_market_or_benchmark). Reporting only the flattering number, omitting the baseline, or hiding the metrics where the baseline beats the model is the cap trigger. (This is a credibility/honesty gate, scored by the Critic; it is NOT a visual_design cap.)
scale_bridge.decorative_or_tonally_wrong_immersion_ca: (UNCHANGED — the valid guard.) A cinematic background or BGM that is DECORATIVE (no INFORM/IMMERSE purpose, bolted on to look rich) or TONALLY WRONG for the subject (a celebratory anthem on a grief/disaster topic, a jarring atmosphere that fights the mood) caps visual_design at 3 — exactly like decorative media (ANT5). Mandatory cinematic + BGM means always-present-AND-tasteful, NEVER force-junk: making the immersion present does not exempt it from this cap. A tonally-wrong forced immersion is STILL capped here.
scale_bridge.inert_immersion_floor_cap: (EXTENDS the richness floor — coexists with `decorative_or_tonally_wrong_immersion_cap`.) Because cinematic + BGM are now MANDATORY stages, an INERT page that ships them EFFECTIVELY ABSENT is the IMPOVERISHMENT failure (the inverse of the decorative cap): CAP visual_design at 3 when the cinematic scroll layer is effectively absent (no scroll background built / a token immersion that does nothing) OR no BGM is present where one fits (a non-privacy topic with no fitting front-of-blog soundtrack). The two caps coexist by design: present-but-tonally-wrong is capped by the decorative cap above; effectively-absent is capped here. REWARD (not cap) a tasteful, topic-appropriate immersion — a real photographic / generative / data_driven scroll background that fits the subject plus a restrained, tonally-fitting real BGM is the positive signal that lifts visual_design toward 5+, not a box ticked. (Privacy_sensitive topics legitimately ship no BGM — the floor does not fire there. The Critic CORROBORATES; the orchestrator gate + validate.py cinematic_missing / bgm_missing own enforcement, and the floor never forces a fabricated/decorative/tonally-wrong asset, which is itself the cap above.)
scale_bridge.multiple_soft_fail: two or more soft fails across groups also cap at 3
scale_bridge.all_hard_pass: eligible for 4+, but the Critic's score_gates still apply: 4 needs >=2 concrete on-page evidence items, 5 needs >=3 plus a design move that carries information the prose does not, 6-7 reference-class. A clean PASS sheet is necessary, not sufficient, for a high score. A clean PASS sheet plus NO signature move (e.g. a stock-default lead chart) is competent visual_design (4), NOT flagship (5+) — see chart_signature_floor and critic R9.
scale_bridge.chart_signature_floor: A chart-led page's lead chart cannot reach visual_design >=5 on a stock-default chart — the signature chart MUST satisfy CHT1 (annotate the datum) AND at least one of CHT2 (direct labels) / CHT3 (de-cluttered axes+units), i.e. it is genuinely the signature_annotated_chart (see abstract_excellence.json + ../../dataviz-craft/references/annotation_layers.json), not a library default. CHT2/CHT3 STAY severity:soft for the FAIL floor (a missing unit does not cap a whole page at 3) but are REQUIRED for the chart-led visual_design 5+ signature move. A cluttered stock-legend chart still PASSES chart_quality (>=4) but cannot be the visual_design signature move (parallels critic R9).
scale_bridge.auditor_routing: A hard fail a vision lens can see is a high-severity Auditor finding routed to designer (design choice) or programmer (render/layout fidelity), matching the Critic visual_design send_back_to.

_sources.use: focus visibility, keyboard operability, touch-target size, motion restraint, transform/opacity-only animation

_sources.name: addyosmani web-quality-skills
_sources.use: Core Web Vitals proxies (CLS via explicit dimensions / reserved heights), accessibility and semantic-structure checks

criteria.rule: Not a single default system font: a display family AND a body family are both set, and neither Inter, Roboto, Open Sans, Lato, Arial, nor system-ui is the ONLY face on the page.
criteria.grep: scan :root for distinct --font-display and --font-body (or distinct font-family stacks on headings vs body); flag if one generic stack covers everything
criteria.vision_hint: headings and body read in visibly different typefaces, not one uniform sans across the whole page
criteria.source: typography.json avoid_fonts ('one system font for everything'); themes.json anti_patterns ('one default system font')

criteria.rule: Visible display-to-body contrast: heading vs body differ in family AND/OR by a weight extreme (100/200 vs 800/900, not 400 vs 600) with a size jump of ~3x+, so the hierarchy reads as deliberate.
criteria.vision_hint: h1 clearly towers over body and looks intentionally paired; adjacent mid-weights at a timid 1.5x step read as accidental and FAIL

criteria.rule: Body measure is ~60-75ch (target 66ch); running prose is not set full page-width edge-to-edge.
criteria.grep: look for max-width on the prose column near 60-75ch / 680-760px; flag full-viewport-width paragraphs
criteria.vision_hint: lines of body text are comfortable length, roughly 9-14 words, not stretching the full window

criteria.rule: No one-word orphan/widow line on a heading; headings use text-wrap:balance (or manual balancing) so multi-line titles break evenly.
criteria.grep: grep for text-wrap:balance on h1/h2 selectors
criteria.vision_hint: two-line headlines split into roughly equal lines; no lone dangling word on its own line

criteria.rule: Numeric columns and aligned stat figures use tabular (lining) numerals so digits align vertically.
criteria.grep: grep for font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums (or font-feature-settings 'tnum') on number/stat/table selectors
criteria.vision_hint: in tables or stacked stats the digits line up in columns rather than drifting

criteria.rule: Palette is themed tokens tied to the subject (heat=warm red/orange, climate=teal, finance=green), driven from :root variables; NOT bootstrap blue and NOT a purple/indigo gradient hero.
criteria.grep: scan :root for subject-tied --accent; flag default bootstrap blue (#007bff/#0d6efd) or a linear-gradient hero in purple/indigo (#6b46c1, #4f46e5, #7c3aed)
criteria.vision_hint: the dominant accent reads as chosen for this story; a purple-to-indigo gradient hero or generic blue FAILS

criteria.rule: ONE coherent data color scale is reused across map, bars and callouts so a color always means one value; charts are NOT on raw Vega/D3 default palettes.
criteria.grep: check Vega-Lite specs set an explicit scale.range / color tied to the theme tokens rather than relying on default schemes
criteria.vision_hint: the same hue means the same quantity everywhere; charts in stock Vega/D3 default colors (the tell: category10 blue-orange-green) FAIL
criteria.source: design_tokens.json data_color_scales _rule; themes.json anti_patterns ('Default chart colors')

criteria.rule: Text meets WCAG AA contrast (>=4.5:1 normal, >=3:1 large), including captions/muted text and any text set on an image (a scrim or solid plate provides the ratio).
criteria.grep: check on-image text sits over a scrim/overlay; spot-check --muted vs --bg
criteria.vision_hint: captions and muted labels are clearly legible; headline text over a photo sits on a darkening scrim, not directly on a busy image
criteria.source: motion.json accessibility.contrast; design_tokens.json color_roles; Vercel web-interface-guidelines

criteria.rule: Categorical encodings are colorblind-safe: categories are not distinguished by hue alone (restrained 4-6 set that also varies in lightness, or backed by direct labels/shape).
criteria.vision_hint: adjacent categories stay distinguishable in a deuteranope/grayscale read; a red-vs-green-only split FAILS

criteria.rule: Accent marks the key datum: the highlighted value carries --accent and the rest is muted, rather than every series fighting for attention in saturated color.
criteria.vision_hint: the eye lands on the one important mark; a chart where all bars/lines are equally bright FAILS
criteria.source: design_tokens.json data_color_scales _rule ('Color the highlighted datum with --accent; mute the rest')

criteria.rule: There is a single clear reading column (~680-760px) for prose; body text is not stretched edge-to-edge across the viewport.
criteria.grep: find a centered content column with max-width ~680-760px and side padding 20-24px
criteria.vision_hint: prose sits in a centered column with margins; text spanning the full window edge-to-edge FAILS

criteria.rule: Full-bleed sections are deliberate and rare (hero, signature map/chart, chapter-break image), implemented via the width:100vw + margin:calc(50% - 50vw) idiom, not the old left:50% hack.
criteria.grep: grep for width:100vw with margin-left:calc(50% - 50vw); flag left:50% translate hacks; flag if most sections are full-bleed
criteria.vision_hint: occasional intentional full-width moments punctuate a mostly-columned page; everything full-bleed reads as no layout system

criteria.rule: The page is NOT a soulless even-card grid with no focal point; there is a clear centerpiece (the lead map, the hero interactive, a hero stat).
criteria.vision_hint: one element clearly anchors the page; a uniform deck of equal cards with nothing dominant FAILS
criteria.source: themes.json anti_patterns ('evenly-spaced soulless cards'); make_it_distinctive ('clear focal centerpiece')

criteria.rule: Section rhythm varies: the visual mode changes between consecutive sections; never 3 charts in a row without a non-chart beat (image, map, stat, quote, interactive).
criteria.vision_hint: scrolling alternates between text, charts, media and stats; three same-looking chart blocks stacked back-to-back FAILS
criteria.source: layout.json section_rhythm.pacing; themes.json anti_patterns ('Walls of equal-weight charts')

criteria.rule: Vertical rhythm is consistent (steps from one space scale, ~34-56px section padding, visual blocks margin ~2rem 0) with hairline dividers between sections.
criteria.grep: check for a consistent spacing scale and hairline top-border (var(--line)) on sections
criteria.vision_hint: spacing between blocks looks regular and intentional; cramped-then-loose erratic gaps FAIL

criteria.rule: In-body figures (images, charts, framed shots) are SIZE-CAPPED to the reading/break-out column, not blown up to fill the viewport. Only deliberate full-bleed moments break to 100vw — the hero and the signature map (and at most a chapter-break image). A wall of oversized in-column images, or every figure stretched edge-to-edge, FAILS.
criteria.grep: flag width:100vw / margin-left:calc(50% - 50vw) on more than the hero + signature map (+ optional one chapter-break image); confirm in-body figures are clamped to the content column or a bounded break-out (e.g. min(1100px,94vw)), not 100vw
criteria.vision_hint: images sit at a calm in-column or bounded break-out size; only the hero and the map go truly full-bleed. Most/every figure full-bleed reads as no layout system
criteria.source: layout.json full_bleed (rare + deliberate) + break_out_wider; components.json figure (max-width:100%); cf pitfalls.json PIT-02 (over-wide centering)

criteria.rule: Decorative overlay layers (ability chips, particle canvases, flourishes) set pointer-events:none AND carry NO data-* traceability tag — so they never swallow clicks meant for the interactive/Verify layer beneath them, and never become a spurious Verify hit-target.
criteria.grep: for each absolutely/fixed-positioned overlay above an interactive region, confirm pointer-events:none and the absence of any data-(edt|des|ana|sct|cin|det|int)= attribute; only real content/controls get pointer events + data-* tags
criteria.source: pitfalls.json PIT-41 (decorative overlay eats clicks / spurious verify target); exemplars/cinematic_flagship.md E1; cf PIT-12 (real modules need resolvable data-*)

chart_quality._ref: auditor SKILL.md (charts lens, render report); analyst.json encodings

criteria.rule: The key datum is annotated directly on the chart (a label, callout or marker on the relevant point), not left for the reader to find.
criteria.vision_hint: the chart points at its own punchline with an on-canvas annotation; a bare chart with no highlighted takeaway FAILS
criteria.source: themes.json anti_patterns ('no hierarchy, captions or annotation'); critic rubric visual_design

criteria.rule: Series are labelled directly (labels at the end of lines / on bars) in preference to a separate legend, where the chart type allows it.
criteria.vision_hint: line/area series carry inline end-labels rather than forcing a legend-to-color lookup
criteria.source: addyosmani web-quality-skills (chart legibility); analyst encoding guidance

criteria.rule: Axes are de-cluttered (no redundant gridlines/ticks) and units are stated (axis title or label carries the unit).
criteria.vision_hint: axes are clean and every quantitative axis names its unit; dense default gridlines or unlabelled axes FAIL

criteria.rule: The chart type fits the encoding: no pie chart for a time series, no misleading dual-axis, categorical vs continuous handled correctly.
criteria.grep: cross-check the Vega-Lite mark vs the field types in analyst.json (temporal -> line/area, nominal parts-of-whole -> bar not pie, no twin independent y-axes)
criteria.vision_hint: the visual form matches the data relationship; a pie for trend-over-time or a two-scale dual axis implying false correlation FAILS
criteria.source: critic rubric claim_data_alignment ('a headline number contradicted by its own chart'); analyst.json

criteria.rule: Every chart actually renders with non-zero width/height (it is visible to a reader, not a blank/0px mount).
criteria.grep: cross-link the Auditor render report: zeroWidthCharts / zeroHeightCharts / chartsWithNoRender / hiddenCharts must be empty
criteria.vision_hint: each chart region shows a drawn chart in the screenshot, not an empty box
criteria.source: auditor SKILL.md Step 0 (render_report findings); component_implementations.json charts_vega_lite (width:container measured after layout, reserved height)

motion._ref: motion.json (tokens + choreography + reduced_motion + anti_slop_checklist); kylezantos design-motion-principles

criteria.rule: prefers-reduced-motion is respected: a media query disables non-essential transitions/animations and any autoplay motion, and the page is fully usable static.
criteria.grep: grep for @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) that actually neutralizes animation/transition (e.g. animation:none / transition:none)

criteria.rule: No autoplay sound; any audio element exposes play/pause controls; ambient/background video is muted (and has a poster).
criteria.grep: flag <audio autoplay> without controls; flag <video autoplay> without muted; check controls present on audio
criteria.vision_hint: no sound starts on load; an audio block shows a control affordance

criteria.rule: No AI-slop pulsing/glow: no perpetual @keyframes pulse/glow with animation:...infinite on indicators, badges or CTAs.
criteria.grep: grep for @keyframes (pulse|glow|shimmer) combined with animation: ... infinite on buttons / CTAs / status dots

criteria.rule: No motion-on-mount for static content: headings, paragraphs and nav do not animate in just because the page loaded (scroll-reveal of sections as a deliberate device is allowed).
criteria.grep: flag entrance/fade-in/translate animations bound to load on h1/h2/p/nav rather than to an IntersectionObserver scroll-reveal

criteria.rule: No uniform fade-in / hover-scale / stagger spam; animate only transform and opacity, never transition:all; motion is subtle (8-16px, ~200-500ms).
criteria.grep: flag transition:all; flag every element sharing one fade-in or hover:scale; confirm transitions target transform/opacity with bounded duration
criteria.source: Vercel web-interface-guidelines (animate transform/opacity, avoid transition:all); kylezantos design-motion-principles; motion.json anti_slop_checklist (restraint)

criteria.rule: No reveal/scroll-animation that hides content on load: content is visible by default; any opacity:0 reveal state is gated behind a JS-added root class (e.g. html.js-reveal) and applies ONLY to below-the-fold, non-visual elements — never charts/maps/visuals, never above the fold. A bare `.reveal > *{opacity:0}` un-hidden only by an IntersectionObserver fails: async visuals stay blank and, with JS slow/off, nothing un-hides, yet the box still measures non-zero so render checks miss it.
criteria.grep: flag any opacity:0 reveal initial state not gated behind a JS root class, or applied to figure/[data-vis]/.chart, or covering above-the-fold content (content invisible on load)
criteria.source: motion.json choreography.reveal_visible_by_default; kylezantos design-motion-principles; surfaced by the data2story e2e Auditor render-vs-source catch

accessibility._ref: motion.json accessibility; addyosmani web-quality-skills; Vercel web-interface-guidelines

criteria.rule: Meaningful images have descriptive alt text, purely decorative images have alt="", and icon-only buttons carry an aria-label.
criteria.grep: check every has alt; decorative ones alt=""; icon
criteria.vision_hint: (source-led) images convey their subject; cannot fully verify alt from a screenshot

criteria.rule: Interactive elements show a visible focus indicator (>=2px, sufficient contrast); outline:none is never used without an equivalent replacement.
criteria.grep: flag outline:none / outline:0 without a replacement :focus / :focus-visible style; confirm a >=2px focus ring exists
criteria.vision_hint: (probe) a focused control shows a clear ring in the after-screenshot

criteria.rule: Interactives are keyboard-operable via real semantic controls (button / a / input), with a logical tab order; no click handlers on bare div/span standing in for buttons.
criteria.grep: flag onclick on div/span used as a control; confirm buttons/links/sliders are real elements; check tabindex misuse
criteria.vision_hint: (probe) the interaction can be driven and the _probe_after.png differs from _probe_before.png

criteria.rule: Document structure is semantic: one h1, hierarchical h1-h6 without skipped levels, lang set on <html>, and charts/maps carry an aria-label or caption.
criteria.grep: check <html lang=...>; single h1; no skipped heading levels; aria-label/figcaption on chart and map containers
criteria.vision_hint: heading sizes imply a sane outline; chart/map regions are described

criteria.rule: Touch targets for controls (buttons, audio play, slider handles, card-deck arrows) are at least 44x44px.
criteria.grep: check control min-width/min-height or padding yields >=44x44px hit area
criteria.vision_hint: tap controls look comfortably large, not tiny

criteria.rule: No purple/indigo gradient hero on a near-white background (the canonical generic-AI hero).
criteria.grep: flag a linear-gradient hero using purple/indigo stops (#6b46c1, #4f46e5, #7c3aed, #8b5cf6) over a near-#fff page
criteria.vision_hint: the opening section does not read as the stock purple-gradient SaaS hero

criteria.rule: Not everything centered: there is deliberate asymmetry / a real focal point, not every block center-aligned by default.
criteria.vision_hint: alignment varies with intent (off-center hero, asymmetric splits); a page where every element is center-aligned FAILS

criteria.rule: No generic even-card grid as the DOMINANT device; there is one signature centerpiece instead of a wall of identical cards.
criteria.vision_hint: the page's main move is a distinctive centerpiece, not a repeated equal-card grid as the primary structure
criteria.source: themes.json anti_patterns ('evenly-spaced soulless cards'); make_it_distinctive ('clear focal centerpiece')

criteria.rule: Default-font tell: flag Inter, Roboto, Open Sans, Lato, Arial, or system-ui used as the SOLE typeface of the page.
criteria.grep: scan font-family stacks; flag a single Inter/Roboto/Open Sans/Lato/Arial/system-ui stack covering both headings and body
criteria.vision_hint: headings and body are not one undifferentiated default sans
criteria.source: typography.json avoid_fonts; themes.json anti_patterns ('one default system font')

criteria.rule: Applied-regardless-of-subject test: flag the look if it is one of the three current AI clusters (cream+serif+terracotta; near-black+acid-accent; broadsheet-hairlines) AND the subject did not call for it; also no emoji bullets, no lorem/filler text, and no decorative media that declares no INFORM or IMMERSE purpose.
criteria.grep: flag emoji used as list bullets; flag lorem ipsum / placeholder text; check each media asset's designer.json purpose is INFORM or IMMERSE
criteria.vision_hint: the aesthetic fits THIS subject rather than being a portable trend skin clamped onto it; no emoji-bulleted lists; no filler copy
criteria.source: Anthropic frontend-design (three-AI-cluster / applied-regardless-of-subject test); critic rubric ethos (every asset earns INFORM/IMMERSE)
